position_language.md.tongue: the office of holding a tongue at all: the root every language in this package hangs from
position_language.md.note: Written here, not carried in from a culture. The package needed one root - khai's engine contract requires exactly one, and twenty-three siblings have none among them - and the honest root is the office itself: what any language gives whoever holds it, what its grammar makes them mark, what it cannot say, and how it sorts the world for them. It names the five channels of `@chbrain/khai-engine-language` in prose without linking them, because the hard dependency that would let it link them is a later step.

de/position_language_de.md.tongue: German as such, of which every de_* here is a variety
de/position_language_de.md.note: Written here, not carried in from a culture. It holds what every German variety shares, which is where that material always belonged: the varieties found thin in the Länder walk were thin because they were spending their four chapters on the language and had nothing left for themselves. With an anchor to carry the compound noun, the four cases, the sentence bracket and the Sie/du decision, a variety is free to say only what is its own.

en/position_language_en.md.tongue: English as such, of which every en_* here is a variety
en/position_language_en.md.note: Written here, not carried in from a culture. It holds what every English variety shares, which is where that material always belonged: the varieties found thin in the Länder walk were thin because they were spending their four chapters on the language and had nothing left for themselves. With an anchor to carry the lost inflection, the doubled lexicon, the word order that is the grammar and the one second person, a variety is free to say only what is its own.

es/position_language_es.md.note: Written here, not carried in from a culture. It holds what every Spanish variety shares, which is where that material always belonged: the varieties found thin in the Länder walk were thin because they were spending their four chapters on the language and had nothing left for themselves. With an anchor to carry the agreement, the subjunctive, the person carried in the verb and the tú/usted decision, a variety is free to say only what is its own.

de/position_language_de_de_bb.md.tongue: Brandenburg Standard German, on the East Low German floor of the Mark, pulled toward Berlin
de/position_language_de_de_bb.md.note: Written out after the walk found it thin. It now says what it stands on, the East Low German the Mark spoke before it went High German, and what it kept: the j for initial g that grows with nearness to the city, and the landscape words Fließ, Luch and Kietz, the last Slavic like the -ow and -itz place names. Its Loses is the honest one: the variety loses its own contour to Berlinisch, because the features it carries are heard as Berlin outside the Mark. The sorted drift queue reports it FOREIGN for naming Berlin, and the reading is that it does not: every mention is das Berliner Hochdeutsch, der Berliner Klang, das Berlinische, a neighbouring tongue and not a city's institutions. Naming another variety is what a variety is for, the same allowance Ceutan Spanish gets for the speech of the Campo de Gibraltar. Left standing deliberately; the queue is a review queue, not a verdict.

de/position_language_de_de_be.md.tongue: Berlin Standard German, over the Metrolekt of a Low German city that went High German and kept the old sounds
de/position_language_de_de_be.md.note: Written out after the walk found it thin. It had four chapters of Standard German and nothing of Berlin; it now carries what the variety actually has - the unshifted ick, det, wat, Kopp and Pund, the j for initial g, the contracted ooch and een - and the one thing that is grammar rather than sound, the collapse of dative and accusative into a single form, which the sentence denying it performs. The Schnauze is in it as a register the tongue holds, a speech setting in which a stranger may be addressed without preamble, never as a temperament of the people who speak it, because that would be a claim about a culture. Rewritten in this batch: it was claiming ick, det, wat, Kopp, jut, ooch and the case merger as things the Berlin *standard* has, which is the fault Bavaria's file had before Bairisch was split out - the better-known name standing in for the actual tongue. Those features moved to `de/position_language_de_x_brl.md`, where they belong, and what stays here is what actually survives into the regional standard: a vocabulary (Schrippe, Stulle, Pfannkuchen, Sonnabend), the Schnauze register, the dial between the two, and the hypercorrection the merger underneath leaves behind in speakers who reach for the distinction consciously.

de/position_language_de_de_bw.md.tongue: the Standard German of Baden-Württemberg, coloured by Swabian and Badisch
de/position_language_de_de_bw.md.note: Read against the mnemonic on the way through: it names itself and describes its own internal variation, which is the tongue's business, so nothing was cut.

de/position_language_de_de_by.md.tongue: Bavarian Standard German, one state language over three mutually foreign dialect floors
de/position_language_de_de_by.md.note: Read against the mnemonic in the Laender walk and found thin - not generic German but generic Upper German, naming only what it said itself was shared von Bayern bis in die Schweiz. It was then filled with the wrong things: the -l, Stoa, es and enk are Bairisch and not Bavarian Standard German, and they have moved to `bar/position_language_bar.md` where they belong. What stays is true of the regional standard: the southern words it keeps in checked prose, Semmel and Kasten and Sackerl and heuer; the composite past in speech; and the structural fact no other Landeshochdeutsch has, that it lies over three mutually foreign dialect floors, which the play already stages as three positions. All five Bavarian personas hold this standard; three of them hold a dialect as well.

de/position_language_de_de_hb.md.tongue: Bremen Standard German, on a North Low Saxon floor, holding Low German words undeclined
de/position_language_de_de_hb.md.note: Written out after the walk found it thin. Its only local words had been Schifffahrt and Hafenrundfahrt, which are examples of compounding and not features of Bremen speech. It now carries the northern unshifted s before t and p, the spitze Stein the north knows itself by and is losing, and the Low German words that survive in the standard - lütt, schnacken, Deern, buten and binnen, and the Butenbremer that cannot be formed without them. Its sharpest chapter is Orders: those words enter the High German sentence undeclined, so the sentence carries two languages and only one grammar.

de/position_language_de_de_he.md.tongue: Hessian Standard German, gell? and a case system that collapses in the mouth
de/position_language_de_de_he.md.note: Read against the mnemonic on the way through: three clauses were cut. It explained its own register switch by die Bank und die Börse in Frankfurt, by the Protokoll der Bank, and by the move zwischen Wirtshaus und Kontor - a city's finance industry, which the play stages as its own position and place. The register itself is the tongue's business and stays: the same speaker separates the cases or lets them fall together according to how binding the sentence has to be. What it holds is untouched and good: gell? as a particle that appends assent without rebuilding the sentence, hawwe for haben, and the dative and accusative merging into one form in the mouth while the writing keeps four.

de/position_language_de_de_hh.md.tongue: the Standard German of Hamburg, over a Low German floor
de/position_language_de_de_hh.md.note: Read against the mnemonic on the way through: it names itself and describes its own internal variation, which is the tongue's business, so nothing was cut.

de/position_language_de_de_mv.md.tongue: Mecklenburg-Vorpommern Standard German, learned late and laid over Platt
de/position_language_de_de_mv.md.note: Read against the mnemonic on the way through: one clause was cut, and the sorted drift queue is what found it. It said its clear pronunciation once counted as the norm für ganz Deutschland, naming the culture above rather than the standard itself; it now says it served the Bühnenaussprache as a model and entered the checked Hochlautung from there, which is the same fact told about the language. What stayed is the industries its maritime lexicon is losing ground to, because that is a cause of lexical loss and so belongs to Loses, the same shape kept in Ceutan Spanish.

de/position_language_de_de_ni.md.tongue: Lower Saxon Standard German, the High German that lies over a Low German floor
de/position_language_de_de_ni.md.note: Read against the mnemonic on the way through: it names itself and the language beneath it, which is the tongue's own business, so nothing was cut. It is the strongest of this batch, because it explains its own unmarkedness by the substrate it was laid over.

de/position_language_de_de_nw.md.tongue: North Rhine-Westphalian Standard German, carrying the rheinische Verlaufsform
de/position_language_de_de_nw.md.note: Read against the mnemonic on the way through: nothing was cut. It holds two speech regions under one label and says so, which is a tongue describing its own internal variation.

de/position_language_de_de_rp.md.tongue: Rhineland-Palatinate Standard German, Palatine softness under the standard
de/position_language_de_de_rp.md.note: Read against the mnemonic on the way through: one clause was cut. Its sound was said to give the Winzerstube its warmth, which is what a room in a culture gets, not what a tongue does to whoever holds it. It now says what the diminutive does to everything it names.

de/position_language_de_de_sh.md.tongue: Schleswig-Holstein Standard German, the closest to the stage pronunciation because no High German dialect colours it
de/position_language_de_de_sh.md.note: Read against the mnemonic on the way through: one epithet was cut. It said im Land zwischen den Meeren, and where is not one of the four chapters, the same cut Ceutan and Melillan Spanish took. Everything else is the office, and its central claim is a good one: this standard stays near the taught sound precisely because there is no local High German dialect to colour it, only a different language underneath.

de/position_language_de_de_sl.md.tongue: the Standard German of the Saarland, on a Rhenish-Franconian base beside French
de/position_language_de_de_sl.md.note: Read against the mnemonic on the way through: it names itself and describes its own internal variation, which is the tongue's business, so nothing was cut.

de/position_language_de_de_sn.md.tongue: Saxon German, the Meissen chancery sound that helped found the written standard
de/position_language_de_de_sn.md.note: Read against the mnemonic on the way through: nothing was cut. Every chapter is the office - the lenition, the drawn-out melody, the switch between the home sound and the sharper written one.

de/position_language_de_de_st.md.tongue: Saxony-Anhalt German, the Anhalt and Mansfeld sound that fed the chancery language
de/position_language_de_de_st.md.note: Read against the mnemonic on the way through: nothing was cut. The soft stops, the long simple vowels where the writing sets a diphthong, and the descent of the written standard from this landscape's chancery language are all the office. It names the industries its lexicon is losing ground to, which is a cause of lexical loss and belongs to Loses, the shape kept since Ceutan Spanish.

de/position_language_de_de_th.md.tongue: Thuringian German, singing and soft, and closest of all to the standard it helped make
de/position_language_de_de_th.md.note: Read against the mnemonic on the way through: nothing was cut. Its Loses is the sharpest in the batch and is entirely about itself - it loses its distinctness precisely where it stands nearest the standard, because dialect and written language grew from the same root, so it dissolves faster than a dialect that started further away.

en/position_language_en_us_oh.md.note: Read against the mnemonic on the way through: it names itself and describes its own internal variation, which is the tongue's business, so nothing was cut.

en/position_language_en_us_pa.md.note: Read against the mnemonic on the way through: it names itself and describes its own internal variation, which is the tongue's business, so nothing was cut.

en/position_language_en_us_va.md.tongue: Virginian English, the drawl and the second-person plural English otherwise lost
en/position_language_en_us_va.md.note: Read against the mnemonic on the way through: it names itself and describes its own internal variation, which is the tongue's business, so nothing was cut.

es/position_language_es_es_ce.md.tongue: Ceutan Spanish, Andalusian in its sounds and full of Darija that nobody hears as borrowed
es/position_language_es_es_ce.md.note: Read against the mnemonic on the way through: it opened by placing itself on the African shore of the Strait, and where is not one of the four, so it now names the community that speaks it instead. Everything else is the office: the Darija it holds without translating, the register it forces at the official counter, the maritime lexicon it is losing with the trades.

es/position_language_es_es_ml.md.tongue: Melillan Spanish, close to the standard and carrying the complete vocabulary of accreditation
es/position_language_es_es_ml.md.note: Read against the mnemonic on the way through: two things were cut from its opening. It placed itself on the Rif coast, and where is not one of the four; and it explained its own closeness to the standard by who lives in the city, its garrison and its civil service, which is a claim about a place and not about a tongue. What stays is the strongest thing it says: that it orders its holder to state where they are from and since when before saying what they want.

nds/position_language_nds.md.tongue: Low German, the northern branch that never took the High German consonant shift
nds/position_language_nds.md.orthography: SASS-Schreibung, carried in and not verified against the norm
nds/position_language_nds.md.note: Read against the mnemonic on the way through: nothing was cut, and it is the cleanest position in the package. Written in Low German itself. Every chapter is the office: the unshifted p, t and k that keep Water from becoming Wasser, two noun forms where High German holds four, the verb in second place even where High German would hold it back, and no settled orthography, so a language that once ran from Bruges to Novgorod still looks for one rule to write itself by. Note that this is a language and not a variety of German - `language: nds`, registered in the house's `khai.languages` - and that it is held here by one Land while Hamburg, Bremen, Lower Saxony and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern all name Platt in their own varieties without linking it. Now that it sits in the package they could, by specifier; that is a later pass and not this one.

rif/position_language_rif.md.tongue: Tarifit, the Riffian Amazigh of the Rif coast
rif/position_language_rif.md.orthography: Latin script, Rif writing practice, carried in from es_melilla
rif/position_language_rif.md.note: Written in Tarifit in Latin script, the convention of Riffian writing in Morocco and the diaspora; Tifinagh, official in Morocco since 2003, is not used in the city it came from. Registered as `rif` in the house's `khai.languages`, which routes it to assisted verification instead of the local detector. Read against the mnemonic when it moved here: two claims about Melilla, its households and its schools, were cut, because a position says what a tongue does to whoever holds it and not what a city does about it. The Rif stays, as the speech community that holds the tongue.

bar/position_language_bar.md.tongue: Bavarian as such: the family, spoken across three states and owned by none of them
bar/position_language_bar.md.note: Written here as the anchor the family needed. The file that carried this name held Munich's Mittelbairisch under the family's title - the same mistake das bayerische Hochdeutsch was making with Bairisch features - so its content moved down to `bar_mitt` and the anchor was written fresh. What belongs at family level is what every Bairisch variety shares: the -l, the article before a name, es and enk from the old dual, and the missing preterite. Its strongest chapter is Loses, and it is the reason this package exists: Bairisch is spoken in Bavaria, Austria and South Tyrol by some fourteen million people, so the same dialect is a Mundart in one state and close to the state language in another - was in Wien fast s Amtsdeitsch is, gilt in München scho ois Bauernsproch.

bar/position_language_bar_mitt.md.tongue: Central Bavarian: the Danube belt, Munich and Vienna both
bar/position_language_bar_mitt.md.orthography: author's own, carried in from de_bavaria
bar/position_language_bar_mitt.md.note: This is the file that used to be the anchor, carrying Munich's variety under the family's name. It now holds only what is Mittelbairisch and not Bairisch in general: the ua and ia reflexes that its northern sibling takes the other way, oa for Stein, and the l-vocalisation that makes Goid of Gold and Woid of Wald. Its Loses is the honest one for a majority variety - it is the one that displaces the others. A speaker who moves from the Oberpfalz to Munich gives up ou and ei within a few years and never the reverse, so Mittelbairisch grows at its neighbours' expense without anyone intending it.

bar/position_language_bar_nord.md.tongue: Northern Bavarian: the Oberpfalz, and the gestürzte Diphthonge
bar/position_language_bar_nord.md.note: Written here; no culture carried it in, because no culture in this house has yet staged the Oberpfalz - which does not bear on whether the tongue exists. Its whole identity is one feature running through every word: the old diphthongs fall the other way. Where Mittelbairisch has Bruada, Buach, liab and miad, Nordbairisch has Brouda, Bouch, leib and meid. Written in Northern Bavarian so the fall is visible rather than described. Its Loses names two pressures and one injury: Mittelbairisch from the south, Ostfränkisch from the north, and the fact that it is heard not as another Bavarian but as Bavarian spoken wrong - though its own reflex often preserves the older form.

vmf/position_language_vmf.md.tongue: East Franconian: no hard consonants, -la, and a gendered two
vmf/position_language_vmf.md.orthography: author's own, carried in from de_bavaria
vmf/position_language_vmf.md.note: Came here as `position_fraenkisch.md`, an ordinary position titled "The Franconian Language Variety" tagged `language: de`, the sibling of the Bairisch file with the same fault: 102 words whose Has offered one real feature and two gestures, and whose Orders stated a cultural duty - dass man die Mundart pflegt - where a language position must state what the grammar forces. Rewritten to the mnemonic and written in Franconian. It carries the lenition that makes Gonsonanden of Konsonanten, the -la diminutive that is neither Bairisch's -l nor Swabian's -le, and the feature worth the most: East Franconian still genders the numeral two - zwee Männer, zwo Fraan, zwaa Kinner - which Standard German lost entirely. Its Loses is that it is heard as Bavarian from outside, because state membership travels further than language family. Exempt: franc has no vmf model.

swg/position_language_swg.md.tongue: Swabian as such: the anchor, and its heartland is in another state
swg/position_language_swg.md.note: Written here as the anchor. Swabian's centre is Württemberg, so this tongue was a cross-border speech community before the package had a word for one, which is the clearest case yet for holding tongues apart from countries. It carries the sch before consonant that gives it away in the first sentence, the -le, the -a endings, the nasal vowels, and the composite past it shares with all Upper German. Its Loses names the seam it sits on: no sharp boundary to Alemannic, so the further south, the longer Huus stays Huus instead of becoming Hous.

swg/position_language_swg_by.md.tongue: Bavarian Swabian: Swabian on the wrong side of the state border
swg/position_language_swg_by.md.orthography: author's own, carried in from de_bavaria
swg/position_language_swg_by.md.note: Came here as `position_bayerisch_schwaebisch.md`, 100 words from the same template as the Franconian and Bairisch files, with a cultural duty for an Orders. Rewritten to the mnemonic, and narrowed: it is Augsburg and the Donau-Ries, Swabian with Bairisch as its neighbour rather than as its overlord. Sepp, its only holder, does not speak this - he is an Älpler in the Allgäu, and he moves to the Allgäu variety, so this file has no holder in the house and is none the worse for it.

swg/position_language_swg_allgaeu.md.tongue: Allgäu Swabian: the variety standing on the Swabian/Alemannic line
swg/position_language_swg_allgaeu.md.note: Written here. The Allgäu is where Swabian stops being Swabian: the New High German diphthongisation that made Hous of Huus runs out partway down the valley, and south of that the old monophthong stands, as it does in Vorarlberg and Switzerland. That isogloss crosses no other Bavarian region. Its own word marks it - d Alp and d Alpe, not d Alm, and whoever says Alm is not from here. Sepp holds this rather than the Augsburg variety he was filed under, which was the Bairisch mistake in miniature: the better-known name standing in for the actual tongue.

de/position_language_de_x_hes.md.tongue: Rhine Franconian of the Untermain: Hessian inside Bavaria, and the first tongue here with no ISO code
de/position_language_de_x_hes.md.note: Written here. The Bayerischer Untermain around Aschaffenburg speaks Rhine Franconian, which is Hessian and not Franconian at all, despite sitting in Bavaria's Franconian third - the clearest case in the house of a language border that is not a state border. It is the first variety with no ISO 639-3 code: Pfälzisch has `pfl`, Hessian has nothing, and the house refused both to mint a code into the ISO space and to deny a tongue a position because a registry never named it. It carries `language: de-x-hes`, a BCP-47 private-use tag, which khai-language 0.1.25 accepts: `resolveLanguage` returns german so the prose gates against German, while `resolveLanguageTag` keeps de-x-hes so the variety is still named. Verified both ways on this file. It lives under `de/` and not in a directory of its own, because the tag says it is German and the version rule counts languages - a private-use variety must not inflate that count. What it carries: Staa where the writing has Stein and Munich has Stoa, so one word places it between its two neighbours; isch and des; the intervocalic w of hawwe and gewwe; and the -che diminutive against the Bavarian -l and the Franconian -la. Its Loses is that it loses its own name - heard as Hessian because it sounds so, filed as Franconian because it is administered so, and called what it is by almost nobody.

hsb/position_language_hsb.md.tongue: Upper Sorbian: West Slavic, and it still has a living dual
hsb/position_language_hsb.md.note: Written here. Not a German dialect and not written as one: Sorbian is West Slavic and its nearest relatives are Czech and Polish, so nothing in it is stated as a departure from German - that frame is what turns a minority language into a footnote to a majority one. Its Has is the dual, a whole number category for exactly two, surviving on the noun and the verb both, which only a handful of European languages still carry. Its Loses is the office fact that no other tongue here has: it has no monolingual speaker at all, so a conversation can switch at any moment and usually does, and the dual is the first thing younger speakers drop - the tongue loses first what most distinguishes it. Flagged for native review: no Sorbian speaker has read this prose. What can be said is that khai's own gate accepts it as Upper Sorbian, franc topping it hsb at 1.00, which is evidence it reads as the language and not evidence that it reads well.

dsb/position_language_dsb.md.tongue: Lower Sorbian: the smaller of the two, and taught rather than handed down
dsb/position_language_dsb.md.note: Written here, and deliberately not as a variant of Upper Sorbian - they are two languages with two standards, and writing one as a version of the other is the same fault as Munich's Bairisch under the family name. Checked mechanically for exactly that: the file carries five of five Lower markers and none of five Upper ones, where the Upper Sorbian file carries four of five Upper, and the two share 30% of their tokens, which is what two related Slavic languages share rather than what a copy shares. Its Loses is its own and not Upper Sorbian's: transmission in the family largely broke, so most speakers learned it in a nursery or a school rather than from a mother, and every word is learned rather than found. Exempt in `khai.languages`: franc has an hsb model and no dsb model, so Lower Sorbian reads as Upper Sorbian to the detector and there is nothing honest to gate it against. Flagged for native review.

ksh/position_language_ksh.md.tongue: Kölsch: a tongue defined by which sound shifts reached it and which did not
ksh/position_language_ksh.md.orthography: author's own, Kölsch writing practice; not Rheinische Dokumenta
ksh/position_language_ksh.md.note: Written here. Its Has is structural rather than a list of sounds: Kölsch sits inside the Rhenish fan, where the High German consonant shift did not cross as one front but as a sheaf of separate lines, each running its own course. So it says ich and maache with High German and dat, wat and et with Low German - it took from every line what reached it and from none of them everything. Its Orders and its Loses are one feature seen twice: Kölsch has two tones, so two words can carry the same letters and differ only in how the voice holds them, and no writing system it has can record that. A tongue that distinguishes words by pitch and cannot write pitch loses, at every transcription, exactly what distinguishes it - which is the sharpest case in this package of the rule that a feature invisible in writing cannot be exhibited, only described. Exempt: franc has no ksh model. Worth noting what franc does say - deu:1.00 tied with nds:1.00, which is the unshifted dat and wat showing up in the measurement, weak evidence that the prose sits where it claims to.

sxu/position_language_sxu.md.tongue: Upper Saxon: it helped found the written standard and is now judged by it
sxu/position_language_sxu.md.orthography: author's own, Upper Saxon dialect-writing practice
sxu/position_language_sxu.md.note: Written here. It carries two features that run through every word and are both plainly visible in writing: the Entrundung, so that ü, ö and äu are spoken i, e and ee - Bricke, scheen, Beeme - and the lenition that moves p, t and k toward b, d and g until Bagger and Backer sound alike. Its Loses is the one no other tongue here has and it is not about numbers: the Meissen chancery language is part of the foundation of written German, and the region it came from is now the one most often named as speaking German worst, so the tongue is judged by the standard it helped build. That is an office fact and not a sociological aside - it is what holding this tongue costs its holder, every time they open their mouth outside it. Exempt: franc has no sxu model. Checked against Kölsch for bleeding, five of five own markers and none of the other's, twenty percent shared tokens.

wep/position_language_wep.md.tongue: Westphalian: Low German, with the breaking no other Low German has
wep/position_language_wep.md.note: Placed by the rule this batch settled: the directory is the ISO code the file declares, the members tree is composition and not descent, and linguistic descent lives in the prose. So `wep` sits beside `nds` rather than inside it, and its own text says it is Low German. Its Has is the westfälische Briäkunge, a named categorical sound change running through the whole language - iäten and biäter and guet where the rest of Low German has eten and beter and good. Its Loses is doubled and the second half is the interesting one: it loses to High German like all Low German, and it loses again to its own family, because whoever learns Platt learns the northern kind that is in the books and on the radio, and that kind has no breaking. franc reads the file nds:1.00, which is correct and is weak confirmation the prose sits where it claims.

gsw/position_language_gsw.md.tongue: Alemannic: the monophthongs High German lost, across three states
gsw/position_language_gsw.md.orthography: author's own, Alemannic dialect-writing practice; not Dieth-Schreibung
gsw/position_language_gsw.md.note: Placed by the rule this batch settled: the directory is the ISO code the file declares, the members tree is composition and not descent, and linguistic descent lives in the prose. So `gsw` sits beside `swg` in the filesystem even though Swabian is a branch of Alemannic and not its neighbour - the registry makes them siblings, linguistics does not, and the file says so in its own text rather than encoding the registry's error in the structure. Its Has is the old monophthongs, Huus and Zit and Lüt where High German diphthongised, which is a sound state preserved rather than a colour added. Its Loses is that it loses itself to state borders: the same tongue is a dialect to be ashamed of in one country and the educated colloquial in another, and nothing about the sound changes, only the standing. Exempt, and khai refused gsw for detection on measured grounds - this file is evidence for that refusal rather than against it, since franc scores it deu:1.00 with gsw third at 0.98, inside the margin. It is offered to khai as the real Alemannic prose they asked for.

pfl/position_language_pfl.md.tongue: Palatine: Rhine Franconian, which made the sound shift only halfway
pfl/position_language_pfl.md.note: Placed by the rule this batch settled: the directory is the ISO code the file declares, the members tree is composition and not descent, and linguistic descent lives in the prose. Its Has is the half-completed second sound shift - isch and not ich, des and not das, and the intervocalic w of hawwe and gewwe - which it shares with the Untermain file, because both are Rhine Franconian and shared features are supposed to overlap. What separates them is one morpheme: Palatine says -el and Hessian says -che, and the file names its neighbour's ending to mark where it stops, which is the allowance a variety has for naming the tongue next door. Checked: the three shared features appear in both, the -el in Palatine only. Exempt; franc has no pfl model.

de/position_language_de_x_brl.md.tongue: Berlinisch: a Low German city's High German, with the commonest words left unshifted
de/position_language_de_x_brl.md.note: Written here, and split out of the Berlin regional-standard file in the same commit - the same correction Bavaria got, where a `de_de_*` file was carrying a dialect's shibboleths as if they were the standard's. The rule that earns it a file: Berlinisch carries the second sound shift out everywhere except in a closed, short list of the highest-frequency words, which stay unshifted - ick, icke, det, dit, wat, uff, Kopp, Pund. The minimal pair is three-way and clean: `ick mache` here, `ik maak` in Low German, `ich mache` in the standard. Nothing else in the metrolekt is unshifted; machen is never maken. Categorical, because the list is closed, and fully visible in writing. Its second layer is the j for initial g (jut, jehn, Jeld), the contracted diphthongs (ooch, koofen, loofen, een, keen, Beene) and the emphatic -e forms of the city's own rhyme (icke, dette, kieke). Its Orders is that the list is a list and not a rule, so it cannot be read up, only heard - and that dative and accusative fall together into one form, so a sentence that needs the difference has to change language mid-breath. Sourced to the right side: Agathe Lasch, Berlinisch. Eine berlinische Sprachgeschichte (1928), and Hans Meyer, Der richtige Berliner in Woertern und Redensarten (1878), both a history of this metrolekt and not of the region around it. Carries `language: de-x-brl`, a BCP-47 private-use tag on the de-x-hes precedent, and lives under `de/` so it does not inflate the language count. Checked against every German sibling in the package: five own markers present, zero in bar, swg, nds, wep, ksh, sxu, pfl, hes or mos; token overlap 4-11 percent.

de/position_language_de_x_mos.md.tongue: Moselle Franconian: the tongue that says dat Dorf, which is the only one that does
de/position_language_de_x_mos.md.orthography: author's own, Trier-leaning; deliberately not Luxembourgish orthography
de/position_language_de_x_mos.md.note: Written here. The rule that earns it a file is a single two-word formula off the Rhenish fan: Moselle Franconian is the band where the second sound shift reached Dorf but not dat. Its northern neighbour, Ripuarian, says dat Dorp; its southern neighbour, Rhine Franconian, says das Dorf; only this band says dat Dorf. Categorical, textbook, and visible in writing, and the three shipped files test it - the check run for this batch shows dat present in ksh and mos and absent in pfl and hes, and Dorf and Dorp appearing together only in the mos file, where they are the quoted minimal pair. Sourced to Wenker and Wrede's Deutscher Sprachatlas and the Rhenish-fan isoglosses it drew (the dorp/dorf line and the dat/das line). Its Orders is the Eifeler Regel, which no other German variety has: word-final n drops before a consonant and stands before a vowel or d, t, z, h, n, so the speaker must know the next word before finishing the current one. Named honestly as strongest in the north and in Luxembourgish and looser southward, per the entry price's categorical-or-shades-off test. Its Loses is that it has no name of its own - every name it has is a region's or a Land's, and one of them, Saarlaendisch, covers two different tongues because the dat/das line runs through what that name spans. Luxembourgish is named as what this tongue is when it gets a script and a name, which is a tongue-level fact and not a claim about any culture's institutions. Carries `language: de-x-mos`; lives under `de/`. Checked against every German sibling: five own markers present, at most one in any other file and that one is `dat`, which is a genuinely shared northern feature and exactly what the file says is not enough to identify it; token overlap 5-11 percent.

es/position_language_es_es_an.md.tongue: Andalusian Spanish: the open vowel doing the work the lost consonant did
es/position_language_es_es_an.md.note: Read against the mnemonic on the way through: nothing was cut. Every chapter is the office - the aspirated or dropped final s that leaves the vowel open and long to carry the plural on its own, the seseo and ceceo folding two letters into one sound, and the western ustedes that serves as the only plural where the rest of Spanish keeps two. Its Loses is the sharpest of the six: it loses the final consonant itself, and it loses again when that opening is judged as carelessness rather than read as the rule it is.

es/position_language_es_es_ar.md.tongue: Aragonese Spanish: the -ico diminutive and the apocope, and the Aragonese underneath both
es/position_language_es_es_ar.md.note: Read against the mnemonic on the way through: nothing was cut. Its Has opens as a fragment rather than a sentence - `Lo que el castellano de Aragon conserva de la lengua aragonesa que tiene debajo` - which is left standing because it answers the chapter's question directly; the four chapters are the office throughout. It names Aragon as its own subject and not as a culture's institutions, which is the allowance a variety has for identifying itself.

es/position_language_es_es_as.md.tongue: Asturian Spanish: the -in diminutive and the metaphony the Asturian underneath pushes up
es/position_language_es_es_as.md.note: Read against the mnemonic on the way through: nothing was cut. Every chapter is the office - the metaphony closing the final vowels, the -in and -ina against Castilian -ito and -ita, and the mine, sea and brana vocabulary that the Spanish of other regions does not have to hand.

es/position_language_es_es_ib.md.tongue: Balearic Spanish: Castilian grammar carrying a Mallorcan ear it cannot write down
es/position_language_es_es_ib.md.note: Read against the mnemonic on the way through: nothing was cut. Its Loses is the good one and it is precisely stated - the salted article, es and sa, cannot cross into Castilian because Castilian grammar has no slot for it, so the feature stays trapped in the language of the house and never reaches the language of dealings. It names Mallorcan as the tongue next door, which is the allowance.

es/position_language_es_es_cn.md.tongue: Canarian Spanish: seseo, ustedes, and an Atlantic rather than peninsular set of tenses
es/position_language_es_es_cn.md.note: Read against the mnemonic on the way through: nothing was cut. Every chapter is the office. It reaches toward the American varieties rather than the peninsular ones, and says so about the tongue and not about the islands.

es/position_language_es_es_cb.md.tongue: Cantabrian Spanish: the unhurried line and a vocabulary split between the sea and the high pasture
es/position_language_es_es_cb.md.note: Read against the mnemonic on the way through: nothing was cut. Every chapter is the office - the paused intonation, and the double lexicon of boat and cattle that one speaker carries without either half feeling borrowed.

fr/position_language_fr.md.tongue: French as such, of which every fr_* here is a variety
fr/position_language_fr.md.note: Written here, not carried in from a culture, on the pattern the de and es anchors set: it holds what every French variety shares, so a variety is free to say only what is its own. What it carries: the gender that nothing in the thing predicts; the split between a written French that keeps its marks and a spoken French that has dropped them, so parle, parles and parlent are three spellings and one sound; the liaison; the four nasal vowels; the passe simple that lives only on the page; the tu/vous decision with nothing between; and the two-part negation that has to be opened before you know what you are denying. Its Loses is the one that made it worth writing at family level - almost everything the writing distinguishes is inaudible, so number and person are carried by the little word in front and not by the word itself.

it/position_language_it.md.tongue: Italian as such, of which every it_* here is a variety
it/position_language_it.md.note: Written here, on the same pattern. What it carries: the ending that holds the person so the subject pronoun is normally absent; the geminate consonant, which is phonemic and not emphasis - nono and nonno, pala and palla, caro and carro, sete and sette; the vowel-final word; and the suffix scale that builds size and judgement into the noun itself, tavolino, tavolone, tavolaccio. Its Loses names the split that no single Italian variety can settle: the passato remoto is alive in one half of the language and literary in the other, so one form means two different things depending on the mouth.

de/position_language_de_ch.md.tongue: Swiss Standard German: a written form and almost nothing else
de/position_language_de_ch.md.orthography: deutsche Rechtschreibung, schweizerische Variante ohne ß
de/position_language_de_ch.md.note: Migrated and trimmed. Its own throughout: no sharp s anywhere, a vocabulary that comes largely from French rather than German (Velo, Poulet, Trottoir, Billett, Perron), and the position no other national standard has - it is a writing form, spoken only when reading aloud or talking to outsiders. The Orders chapter now says what makes it different from the other diglossias in this package: the switch is not a dial, as it is in Berlin or Vienna, but a toggle, because there is no written dialect that counts in an office and no spoken standard that counts at home.

de/position_language_de_li.md.tongue: Liechtenstein Standard German: a written norm the country did not make
de/position_language_de_li.md.orthography: deutsche Rechtschreibung, schweizerische Variante ohne ß
de/position_language_de_li.md.note: Migrated and rewritten. What stood in it was the anchor's material plus Switzerland's diglossia, which is not its own. Thinned to the fact that actually belongs to it: the smallest German-writing polity holds a written form it did not make, writing like its western neighbour and reading like its northern one, so its Orders includes a decision no other national German has to make - which of two norms a given text follows, since it has none of its own and the two disagree constantly in small things. Below it is Alemannic, and inside that a Walser variety that came over the mountains and kept forms the valley gave up. Its Loses is stated plainly and without complaint: a speech area of thirty-five thousand carries no norm, no dictionary and no orthography, so everything written here is right or wrong by someone else's measure.

fr/position_language_fr_ch.md.tongue: Swiss French: septante and nonante, and the meals a word earlier
fr/position_language_fr_ch.md.note: Migrated, and the accents restored. It arrived written with no diacritics at all - le francais de Suisse, la ou, dejeuner - and French without accents is not French, so it was rewritten with them. Substance kept and sharpened: septante, nonante and huitante, which say the tens in one transparent word without a base twenty; and dejeuner, diner and souper, which name the morning, midday and evening meals, one notch off from the French of France, so the same word does not mean the same hour on the two sides of the border. Its Orders was thinned - it opened by restating the anchor's gender and subjunctive - and now says what only this variety orders: its own numerals are what has to be written at school and in the press, and a child who writes soixante-dix is corrected.

it/position_language_it_ch.md.tongue: Swiss Italian: a minority twice over, and in two different directions
it/position_language_it_ch.md.note: Migrated and thinned; its Has and Orders both opened by restating the anchor. What it keeps is its own: words that are wholly Italian and yet local (azione for a discount offer, natel for a mobile phone, naturale for still water, riservare for prenotare), which do not feel like borrowings until you cross a border. What it gained is the statement of its actual position, which the file had not made: it is the smallest of the three languages of its own country and the periphery of its own language at once, a minority in two directions. Its Orders follows from that - administrative text arrives already written in German or French and has to be rendered rather than invented, so a new word enters by translation and not by use.

rm/position_language_rm.md.tongue: Romansh: five written idioms and a sixth made to hold them together
rm/position_language_rm.md.note: Migrated with nothing cut; it needed nothing. Written in Romansh, and it is its own anchor, since rm is the ISO code the file declares. Every chapter is the office: the older Latin forms it keeps that its Romance neighbours dropped; the demand that each valley keep its own written idiom while Rumantsch Grischun serves where a Romansh readable outside the valley is needed; the yearly loss of words to German wherever a technical or administrative term arrives that the valley never had; and the loss of unity between the valleys, because five written idioms are not always mutually readable without patience. Exempt from detection - rm was already on the house's khai.languages list.

bar/position_language_bar_wien.md.tongue: Viennese: Middle Bavarian with one vowel moved, and a vocabulary the countryside never had
bar/position_language_bar_wien.md.note: Written here. It exists because two Austrian personas said they spoke Wienerisch and linked the Austrian *standard* - the same fault Bavaria's and Berlin's files had before Bairisch and Berlinisch were split out, the better-known name standing in for the actual tongue. The rule that earns it a file is the Wiener Monophthongierung: where rural Middle Bavarian keeps the diphthong, Vienna has a long a. The minimal pair is clean and famous in both directions - oans zwoa drei against ans zwa drei, Stoa against Staa, hoass against haass - and it runs through every word carrying that vowel. Visible in writing, and the whole Viennese dialect literature is written with it. The second layer is lexical and belongs to no other Bairisch: Powidl, Buchtln, Kolatschn from Czech, Beisl and Hawara from Yiddish, Fiaker and Trafik from further off, words the city drew in because the monarchy came to it. Deliberately NOT claimed: the l-vocalisation (Goid, Woid, Soiz), which bar_mitt already holds and which is Middle Bavarian and not Viennese - the check for this batch confirms none of those three forms appears in this file; the -erl diminutive, which is de_at's; and es/enk, which is the bar anchor's. The Meidlinger L is named in the Has and explicitly not claimed, because it is a phonetic realisation and the house rule is that a difference which is only sound cannot carry a text file. Writing it also turned up an error in a shipped file: bar_mitt claimed Munich and Vienna spoke `dieselbe Sortn` and gave both the oa, which is wrong about Vienna. bar_mitt now says the eastern end takes the oa one step further to the long a, so the two files agree and the correction is where the mistake was. The research came back and three things in the first draft were wrong, so the file was corrected before it merged. First, the monophthongisation is NOT categorical: it is variable and socially stratified, present when a speaker goes broad and receding when they pull in, and the same person does it both ways inside one conversation. Notably it is also not a youth recession - younger Viennese speakers still produce the monophthongised forms (Moosmueller and Enzinger 2015), so the file says the ladder and does not say the tongue is dying. The Orders chapter, which had demanded the monophthong, now says the opposite and truer thing: it does not demand the vowel, it demands that you know what the vowel says about you. Second, the lexical claim was an exclusivity claim and exclusivity is wrong. Powidl, Beisl, Tschick, Hawara, Trafik, Haeferl and Gschropp are Austrian, Bavarian or wider Habsburg-contact vocabulary, culturally dense in Vienna but not Vienna's alone; only Fiaker is safely Vienna-specific. The file now says so in its own text and states what the real distinction is - not that the city has words the countryside lacks, but that all of them arrived in one place at once, because the city drew in the languages they came from. Third, the monophthongisation covers both inherited diphthongs and the first draft claimed only one; Haus to Haaas was added. The contrast was also reframed: it is Vienna against the surrounding East Middle Bavarian countryside, not Vienna against Munich. The Meidlinger L handling was confirmed correct - a phonetic realisation, not a writable contrast. bar_mitt's correction was softened to match: the eastern end takes the oa one step further oft, not always.

sl/position_language_sl.md.tongue: Slovene as such: the dual, and six cases
sl/position_language_sl.md.note: Migrated with nothing cut; it needed nothing. Written in Slovene, and it is its own anchor since sl is the ISO code the file declares. Its Has leads with the feature that earns it at family level and that most of its Slavic relatives gave up: the dual, a grammatical number for exactly two, marked on noun, pronoun and verb alike - midva, midve, sva. Six cases, and a dialect spread the file describes honestly as wider from village to village than many larger languages manage between whole provinces. Migrated in this batch because Austria needs to cast it: Article 7 of the Staatsvertrag guarantees the Carinthian Slovene community its language, and the research settled that what that community writes is Standard Slovene and not a separate Carinthian written norm, so sl is the right file and the Carinthian part belongs in Austria's prose.

hr/position_language_hr.md.tongue: Croatian as such, of which Burgenland Croatian will be a variety
hr/position_language_hr.md.note: Migrated with nothing cut. Written in Croatian, its own anchor. Migrated now rather than later because it is the anchor Burgenland Croatian will hang from: gradiscanskohrvatski has cleared the entry price on research - a codified written norm with writable diagnostics against the standard, ca against sto, va lozi against u lozu, the ikavian ric and dite - but it is not written yet, because writing a variety needs authored prose in it to work from and none has been obtained. The directory is here and the file is not, which is the honest state.

de/position_language_de_at.md.tongue: Austrian Standard German: the same grammar with another vocabulary, and one different auxiliary
de/position_language_de_at.md.note: Migrated and thinned. Its opening clause restated the anchor (`traegt dieselbe Wortbau- und Kasusfaehigkeit wie das Deutsch ueberhaupt`) and its Orders opened with `wie jedes Deutsch`, which is exactly the thinness the de anchor was written to cure. What it keeps is its own: Erdapfel, Jaenner, Sackerl, Marille, Paradeiser, Karfiol, the productive -erl, and the soft barely-aspirated onset. What it gained is the grammatical fact it was missing, and it is a real one: the sein-perfect with the verbs of standing, sitting and lying - ich bin gestanden, ich bin gesessen, ich bin gelegen, where the north takes haben. That is a different choice of auxiliary, not a colouring, and it falls due in every second sentence without a speaker ever making it consciously. Two more Orders came with it: the near-total avoidance of the simple preterite in speech, so a narrated sentence cannot be built any other way than it is built; and the title before the name, which puts a rank into the greeting - whoever does not know the title cannot be polite in this language, only vague. Migrating it finishes the German-language tongues of the DACH group except de_de, and it only cost two castings, because the four cultures that would have carried the rest were finished in the three batches before this one.

de/position_language_de_de.md.tongue: German Standard German: the unmarked one of the three, and the sharp s
de/position_language_de_de.md.note: Written here, not migrated, because what germany held under this name was not a variety. Its four chapters were the compound noun, the Satzklammer, three genders and four cases, and Sie/du - the anchor's material word for word, wearing a variety's title, which is the thinness the de anchor was written to cure and the costume this house refuses to ship. The old file is retired rather than moved. THE ENTRY PRICE, PAID: the sharp s, categorical and orthographic, which the Swiss standard gave up and this one keeps, so Masse/Maße and in Massen/in Maßen are two written words here and one there. The month names, categorical and codified: Januar and Februar against Jänner and Feber. The perfect auxiliary of the verbs of standing, sitting and lying - habe gestanden, habe gesessen, habe gelegen - categorical in WRITING and gradient in speech, since the south of its own speakers says bin as Vienna and Zurich do, and that gradient is the point of its third Drives rather than an embarrassment to hide. The Fugen-s: Zugverspätung against Zugsverspätung, Schweinebraten against Schweinsbraten. And the fact that carries the Has and the Loses together - it is the variety the dictionaries of the whole language area leave unmarked while they set an A beside Jänner and a CH beside Rahm. Sources: the Variantenwörterbuch des Deutschen (Ammon et al.) for the marked/unmarked codification and the lexical sets; the standard German orthography for the sharp s. RELINKED, and not all to the same place: germany's modern cast (Bismarck, Adenauer, Kohl, Elke, Mehmet, Jonas), its culture-position and its play hold this variety; Luther, Goethe and the 842 origin plot hold the anchor instead, because a national standard cannot be held before there is a nation to mark it against, and Luther is where the written form starts rather than where it is one of three. The twenty-one other cultures that linked the old file held a foreign, inherited or historical German - Hus's German of the powerful cities, Ayşe's children on the telephone, Borges reading, Samuel's grandfather's German at a church supper - and every one of them went to the anchor.

en/position_language_en_gb.md.tongue: British English: the older of the two large written forms, and the marked one
en/position_language_en_gb.md.note: Written here, not migrated, for the same reason de_de was: what united_kingdom held under this name was the language and not a variety of it. Its four chapters were the doubled Germanic-and-Romance vocabulary, the phrasal verbs, the strict word order after the case endings wore away, and the flat you - the en anchor's material, and nothing in it distinguished this variety from any other English. The old file is retired rather than moved. THE ENTRY PRICE, PAID, and all of it survives in writing: the noun/verb spelling pairs a licence/to license and a practice/to practise, which the other large form collapsed, so a distinction is made here in the spelling that has to wait for the grammar there; the bare institution, in hospital against in the hospital and at university against at the university, where the missing article means the purpose rather than the building; agreement by sense with a collective, the committee ARE divided, which is available in every sentence where an organisation takes a verb; the unlearnable spelling list, colour and honour but honorary, centre and theatre but perimeter, travelled and cancelled with the second l; and the absence of gotten, which is a lost DISTINCTION rather than a lost irregular - has got is possession and has gotten is acquisition, and only the first survives here. One rule is deliberately named as unsettled rather than smoothed over: -ise against -ize is not a difference between this variety and the other but a difference INSIDE it, the largest dictionary of the language preferring -ize and most writing in this variety preferring -ise, and both correct here in a way neither is anywhere else. Sources: the Oxford English Dictionary and Fowler's Modern English Usage for the -ize/-ise question and the noun/verb pairs; the standard descriptions of British and American usage for the collective agreement, the bare institution and gotten. RELINKED: united_kingdom's own cast, its culture-position and its play hold the variety, and so does one persona elsewhere - bahrain's Bibby, a Briton abroad who holds it entire as a mother tongue. The other ninety-three cultures held English as a foreign, global or inherited tongue, carried as a tool or worn as an imposition, and all of them went to the anchor: of the one hundred and sixty-seven links to the old file, only two were mother-tongue processes.

it/position_language_it_it.md.tongue: Italian Standard Italian: a standard out of a library, over a second system
it/position_language_it_it.md.note: Written here, not migrated - the third file in a row that turned out to be the language wearing a variety's name. What italy held was pro-drop, the congiuntivo, gender and number agreement and the geminates, all of it the it anchor's material, and the anchor states the geminates better: it has them as a capacity (nono/nonno, pala/palla, caro/carro) where the retired file had them as a loss. THE ENTRY PRICE, PAID, against the one sibling this variety has, it_ch. The unmarked lexicon, codified: cellulare, prenotare, ordinare, farmaco, offerta stand in the dictionaries of the whole area without a marker while natel, riservare, comandare, medicamento and azione carry CH. The passato remoto, which the written norm requires of narrative prose from speakers half of whom no longer say it - alive in the south, extinct in the north, one norm for both, and that gradient is named in the chapter rather than smoothed over, as de_de's haben/bin was. Two facts that are the office rather than a rule: a standard modelled on the written language of three poets of one city, fixed in the sixteenth century and rinsed in the nineteenth, so it was built to be read before it was built to administer; and the second system almost every holder has beside it, a sister language rather than an inflection, which makes closeness a change of language and not a change of tone. And one loss that is this variety's own: there is no accentless Italian to retreat into, the broadcast pronunciation being a diction-school artefact almost nobody holds natively, so a speaker is placed before the sentence ends. Sources: the standard descriptions of the questione della lingua for the literary standard; the Italian variant dictionaries for the CH-marked lexicon. RELINKED by the measured holding: of the links to the old file NOT ONE outside italy was a mother-tongue process - six carried, six half-heard, nine followed, one polished - so italy's own cast holds the variety and the other sixteen cultures hold the anchor.

fr/position_language_fr_fr.md.tongue: French Standard French: an arithmetic in its numbers, and a norm with an address
fr/position_language_fr_fr.md.note: Written here, not migrated - the fourth file in a row that was the language wearing a variety's name, and the fourth time the anchor states the shared material better: it has the nasal vowels and the written-against-spoken split (je parle, tu parles, ils parlent: three spellings, one sound) where the retired file had the subjunctive, gender agreement, tu/vous and liaison, all of it common to every French there is. THE ENTRY PRICE, PAID against the one sibling in this package, fr_ch. The numerals, categorical and codified: soixante-dix, quatre-vingts, quatre-vingt-dix-neuf against septante, huitante, nonante - a vigesimal remnant that makes a speaker do an addition and a multiplication before saying a price. The meals, which are the treacherous kind of difference because it is not another word for the same thing but the same word for another: petit-dejeuner, dejeuner, diner here against dejeuner, diner, souper a few hours away. The unmarked lexicon: portable, serpilliere, sac, promotion, de rien stand without a mention while natel, panosse, cornet, action and service carry one. And the feminisation of job titles, which other standards of this language settled in the nineteen-eighties and this one debated for thirty years and admitted in 2019 - dated, in writing, and the clearest case of what it means that the norm here is decided rather than observed. The office it describes is that last fact generalised: a norm with an address, a company founded to give the language certain rules and still sitting, so that whether a turn of phrase is correct is a question with a written answer rather than a matter of usage. RELINKED, and this one was read culture by culture rather than by counting processes, because unlike de_de, en_gb and it_it it has many foreign mother-tongue holders. Every one of them resolved to the anchor on reading. Prince Eugene of Savoy holds French as a mother tongue and was born in 1663, which is the rule already applied to Luther and Goethe: a national standard cannot be held before there is a nation to mark it against. Haiti's whole cast holds what its own prose calls lang lakoloni an and lang elit la. Mauritius's Chazal holds Mauritian French, the Seychelles' cast holds French beside Creole, and Pushkin, Tolstoy, Ruben Dario and Joyce read or carried it. So france's own cast, its culture-position and its play hold the variety, and fifty-two cultures hold the anchor.

tr/position_language_tr.md.tongue: Turkish as such: agglutination, vowel harmony, and an evidential in every sentence
tr/position_language_tr.md.note: MIGRATED AS THE ANCHOR, not retired and replaced. The four tongues before this one - de_de, en_gb, it_it, fr_fr - were each the language wearing a variety's name, and each was retired because the package already held an anchor that said the same material better. This file is the same kind of thing and the opposite case: it is the Turkish language, correctly written, and the package held no tr anchor at all. Its own frontmatter said so - title "The Turkish Language", declared "Türk dili" - so it was never a variety and only ever a filename. So it moves, and nothing is invented: no tr_tr variety is written, because there is no sibling in this package to distinguish it from and no culture in the house casting a Turkish that is not this one, and this house does not give a file to a variety whose distinguishing feature cannot be named. What it holds is language-wide: the suffix chain that builds evlerimizdekiler out of ev, the vowel harmony that admits no exception and makes a word sound woven from one colour end to end, the verb at the end so the hearer holds the whole sentence before it means anything, and the -mis against -di that makes a speaker mark, in every sentence, whether they saw it or were told. RELINKED: all nine cultures that held it now hold the anchor, and no variety is asserted for any of them. tr_tr was germany's last blocker.

hu/position_language_hu.md.tongue: Hungarian as such: agglutination, vowel harmony, and no grammatical gender
hu/position_language_hu.md.note: Migrated as the anchor, like tr before it. What hungary held was the Hungarian language and not a variety of it - its own frontmatter said "the Hungarian Language" - and the package held no hu anchor. So it moves and nothing is invented: no hu_hu is written, because there is no sibling in this package to distinguish it from and no culture in the house casting a Hungarian that is not this one. Five cultures held it and all five now hold the anchor. It was one of austria's three remaining blockers, which is why it moves now.

la/position_language_la.md.tongue: Latin: six cases, free word order, and no living speech community
la/position_language_la.md.note: Migrated as the anchor. Latin is the widest tongue in this house after en_gb and fr_fr - thirty-seven cultures hold it, and every one holds it as a carried, read or deciphered tongue rather than a mother tongue, which is the one thing that is true of Latin everywhere and of no other tongue here. It is also the clearest case for the package's own rule about who holds a tongue: the tongues package exists because a variety is held by the speech community that speaks it rather than by a country, and Latin has no speech community at all, so it belonged under holy_see even less than the others belonged under theirs. No la_va or ecclesiastical variety is written; the differences between classical and ecclesiastical pronunciation are real but this house ships no file for a variety it cannot distinguish in writing, and the two are one orthography.

cs/position_language_cs.md.tongue: Czech: seven cases, aspect on every verb, and a written form nobody speaks
cs/position_language_cs.md.note: Migrated as the anchor, like tr and hu. What czechia held was the Czech language - seven cases carrying the relations that word order carries elsewhere, and the perfective/imperfective pair on every verb - and the package held no cs anchor. Five cultures held it and all five now hold the anchor. No cs_cz is written: there is no sibling here to distinguish it from. The spisovná/obecná split is a real diglossia and would be a candidate for a variety if a culture in this house ever cast the spoken form as such; none does, and this house does not ship a file for a variety nobody holds.

da/position_language_da.md.tongue: Danish as such: the definite article hung on the back of the word, and the stod
da/position_language_da.md.note: Migrated as the anchor, like tr, hu and cs before it. What denmark held was the Danish language and not a variety of it - its own frontmatter said "the Danish Language", declared "det danske sprog" - and the package held no da anchor. So it moves and nothing is invented: no da_dk is written, because there is no sibling in this package to distinguish it from and no culture in the house casting a Danish that is not this one. What it holds is language-wide and all of it nameable: the postposed definite article, hus becoming huset and bog becoming bogen, so definiteness is baked into the word's own form rather than set in front of it; the stod, a glottal catch that can be the only thing between two otherwise identical words; the free compounding; and the forced choice of faelleskon or intetkon, en or et, before the article can be hung on at all. Read against the mnemonic on the way through and nothing was cut: its Loses is about the spoken form swallowing its own consonants and the mutual intelligibility that costs it with its neighbours on the page, which is the tongue's business and not a country's. Seven cultures held it - denmark, de_schleswig_holstein, faroe_islands, greenland, iceland, norway and sweden - and all seven now hold the anchor. It was de_schleswig_holstein's only blocker.

en/position_language_en_us.md.tongue: American English: the larger written form, and the unmarked one
en/position_language_en_us.md.note: Moved as a variety in the pass before this one - the first tongue here that needed neither retiring nor inventing, already a variety and already correctly named, only ever in the wrong package - and read here, which is why the move was a plain byte-for-byte rename and the reading is its own act. THE ENTRY PRICE, PAID. What the file carried was rhoticity, which is sound and cannot go in a text file, and the productive verbing of nouns, which the other large written form does too; neither separated it from en_gb on the page. What it carries now is what survives in writing: the spelling system that was regularised on purpose, color and center and traveled and defense and catalog, which is a system and not a list; gotten alive as a distinction the other form has lost, he has got a car being possession and he has gotten a car acquisition, two sentences here and one there; the noun/verb spelling pairs collapsed to one, a license and to license against the licence/license en_gb's own file claims, so the two files now agree about the same fact from opposite sides; the obligatory article on the institution, in the hospital where the other form has in hospital for the condition and the hospital for the building; and the singular verb on a collective, the committee is divided against the committee are divided. Each is categorical and each shows on the page. Sources: Webster's An American Dictionary of the English Language (1828) for the spelling regularisations; Merriam-Webster and Garner's Modern English Usage for gotten, the collective agreement and the license/licence pair. READ AGAINST THE MNEMONIC: the General American material was explaining the pressure toward the standard by broadcasting and national schooling, which are a country's institutions and not a tongue's business, and it now names the prestige register the variety carries inside itself. The compounding-and-clipping sentence went to the anchor's account, being true of English and not of this variety. RELINKED, AND THE SECOND HALF OF THE en_gb SWEEP: retiring en_gb moved one hundred and sixty-five of its one hundred and sixty-seven links to the anchor, because the house used to say English by picking a country and most of those cultures meant English as such. Nothing had ever swept this file, so the same fault sat in it untouched. Eight holders said in their own words that they meant the anchor - Bob Marley's "the world's standard English", Can's "the world's and the job's English", Wangari's "the English of her science" in a British colony, Ljubica's "the English of the sanctions" which was NATO's, Stefan's "the English of the emigration" to Austria, Germany or America, Man Naghol's "the tourists' English" where the tourists are Australian, Fukuzawa's eigaku as the successor to rangaku, and de_saxony's Peggy, wearing English for international chip designers - and all eight now hold it. The thirty-four that remain each meet the American one specifically: the United States' own cast, Latin America's English of the north and of the company, the Pacific the United States administered, the Philippines, and the individuals made in America - Bruce Lee, Ilves, Gibran, Morris Chang, and de Gaulle, who names it l'anglais americain and means Roosevelt's.

ru/position_language_ru.md.tongue: Russian as such: aspect on every verb, no article, and no copula in the present
ru/position_language_ru.md.note: Migrated as the anchor, like tr, hu, la, cs and da. What russia held was the Russian language and not a variety of it - its own frontmatter said "the Russian Language", declared "русский язык" - and the package held no ru anchor. So it moves and nothing is invented: no ru_ru is written, because there is no sibling in this package to distinguish it from and no culture in the house casting a Russian that is not this one. What it holds is language-wide: the perfective/imperfective pair that makes a speaker decide, before naming an action, whether it is finished or running; the verbs of motion that carry direction and repetition in the root itself, идти against ходить, ехать against ездить, where other languages add a separate word; the absence of any article, so definiteness must be read off word order and sense; and the present tense with no copula at all, это стол and not это есть стол, the noun left standing bare. Read against the mnemonic on the way through and nothing was cut: every chapter is about the tongue and none of it about Russia. THE WIDEST MOVE SO FAR - fifty-seven files held it, more than any tongue this package has taken in, and it reaches well past the Slavic world, because Russian is the tongue an empire and then a union taught to everyone inside it. All of them now hold the anchor.

cu/position_language_cu.md.tongue: Church Slavonic: the dual number, three past tenses and a vocative, alive in the altar and never in the mouth
cu/position_language_cu.md.note: Migrated with ru, and for the reason la was: this is the Latin case in Cyrillic. A liturgical tongue is not a country's property, it has no speech community at all, and thirteen files held it of which nine are outside russia - belarus, bulgaria, lithuania, moldova, montenegro, romania, serbia and ukraine twice - each reaching into another culture's directory for the language of its own altar. It belonged under russia even less than the others belonged under theirs. Written in itself, in the pre-reform orthography, which is the point of holding a tongue as a position at all: the dual number that говорит of exactly two (очи, уши, руцѣ) where other tongues know only one and many; the aorist against the imperfect against the perfect, so a speaker marks every past action for what kind of past it was; and the vocative, a separate case for addressing whoever is being addressed. Its Loses is the honest one and the file's own best sentence: the dual and the aorist have no place left in living speech, because the Russian born from it collapsed the past tenses into one and kept the dual only in traces (очи, плечи). Read against the mnemonic and nothing was cut. TWO THINGS RECORDED FOR THE NEXT HAND, neither acted on here, because the move is a move. First: this tongue says in its own Drives that a book language can stay alive in the altar having never been alive in the mouth, which is the exact criterion `mother_tongue: false` exists for - and it is not flagged, because la is not flagged either, and Latin is the clearest never-acquired-first tongue in the house at thirty-seven cultures. Flagging one means deciding the other, and that is a judgement of its own rather than a consequence of a file move. Second, and it is what a flag would catch: of the twelve personas holding this tongue, eleven read it at `process_reading_followed` - Nina, Pushkin and Paisij all чита и впитывает - and montenegro's Njegoš alone reads it at `process_reading_mother_tongue`, in a sentence that in the same breath calls it the tongue "свога владичанског чина и службе", of his episcopal office and service, which is a thing acquired and not a first tongue. He is the outlier against the house's own practice, not against a new rule. Fixing him is not cheap: montenegro carries five dead Company entries, so authoring him owes a Montenegro content pass, and that is its own piece of work.

co/position_language_co.md.tongue: Corsican: a polynomic language, where no variety is the norm because none was ever wanted
co/position_language_co.md.orthography: the Corsican usage taught on the island, with ghj and chj
co/position_language_co.md.note: Written here, not carried in from a culture: no culture in this house held Corsican, and none could, because the island has no play yet. Every chapter is the office rather than the map. What it keeps that Tuscan let go, the article from ILLU and the ghj/chj that no neighbour writes the same way; what its grammar makes a speaker mark, the initial consonant that changes with whatever stands before it, so that no word can be said alone, and in the south the cacuminal that puts the speaker's own end of the island into every sentence; what it cannot say, the administrative and technical vocabulary that arrives in French unaltered because Corsican was never an official language for a single day, and the impossibility of speaking it from nowhere, since a tongue without a norm offers nobody a place to hide; and how it sorts the world, by teaching that one's own parlata is one among several equally right, which is what polynomy actually is in the mouth rather than in the literature.

br/position_language_br.md.tongue: Breton: the only Celtic language on the continent, and the one whose speakers had to choose an orthography rather than decline to
br/position_language_br.md.orthography: peurunvan, the unified spelling of 1941 taught in Diwan and most widely written today
br/position_language_br.md.note: Written here, not carried in from a culture: no culture in this house held Breton, and Brittany has no play yet. Every chapter is the office rather than the map. What it gives, the initial mutations that change a word's first letter rather than its last according to what stands before it, the prepositions that inflect for person so that ganin and ganit are one word and not two, vigesimal counting that French around it gave up, and two great varieties, KLT and Vannetais, over which the orthographic argument was fought to three competing answers rather than left unsettled; what its grammar makes a speaker mark, the element in focus, since there is no neutral word order to fall back on and a subject placed before the verb leaves that verb in the third singular however many the subject is, so every sentence declares what its speaker put forward; what it cannot say, itself with one vocabulary, because administration and science arrived in French and the Breton words built to replace them were built by learners, leaving the neo-Breton of the schools and the inherited Breton of the old speakers mutually thin, and because speaking it in Brittany is now always a statement about the language and never merely a way of saying something; and how it sorts the world, by making the join between two words audible so that no word can be lifted out of its sentence, and by requiring the ranking to be settled before the mouth opens rather than repaired afterwards by stress.
